newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 1.4 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 1.4 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares continued to post gains in selective activity on Friday as the market continued its three-week-long rally prompted by political optimism, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 which overcame the major 2,000 barrier in late trade, closed at a new all-time high of 2,027, up 28 points, or 1.4 percent from Thursday's previous record of 1,999.
Daily trade volume declined to 31.31 trillion lira ($206.9 million) from Thursday's 35.77 trillion ($236.9 million).
The market widely expects the new right-left coalition headed by conservative Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz to win a confidence vote in parliament on Saturday.

"Market expectations about the confidence vote will be fulfilled on Monday, so there may be an easing. Afterwards, the government's economic performance and an election date to be set will determine the market direction," said Erden Gokay from Taksim securities.
An MP from Yilmaz's Motherland Party said the government would present a bill on early elections to parliament in the coming days.

The market index has soared 29.5 percent since June 18 when the former Islamist-led coalition government resigned and hopes flared that it would be replaced by a secularist alliance. It hit nine record closes during the rally.
